To give you some insight of what really happened with insurance premiums you have to understand that most healthcare insurance companies are actually the Hospitals themselves. For instance I work for Kaiser Permanente and our members are insured with KP advantage coverages. Sutter and Muir (The other two major California Hospitals) do it exactly the same as Kaiser. Now enters Affordable Healthcare and the state of CA with its Medi-Cal for 'low' income persons. Medi-Cal forced double the normal amount of patients we had been caring for and did not reimburse us the full amount it cost to care for these patients. Our overhead for both operating costs as well as the expansion of facilities for the new volume of patients had to come from somewhere and unfortunately it was pushed to our actual paying patients.

If you were insured by your employer you might have noticed a decrease in coverage or a higher co-pay as the employers downsized their insurance, or if you paid your insurance than you obviously saw the increase in premiums. Meanwhile the poor were once again incentivized and subsidized for poor life choices. Obviously this excludes disabled individuals since they already qualified for Medicare.
